content.value_statement: Email experiments can produce misleading winners when variables, sample sizes, or decision rules are unclear. This skill creates powered test plans and structured result read-outs.
actual_capabilities: Designs A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out email experiments.
Creates falsifiable hypotheses with controls and isolated variables.
Estimates sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, and power from user baselines.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for each experiment mode.
Evaluates rate or continuous outcomes with documented statistical methods and uncertainty.
Applies only precommitted, owner-approved action rules and otherwise returns an undecided result.
limitations: It does not write subject lines, email bodies, calls to action, or other creative.
It requires user-provided baselines, send volumes, or finished experiment exports.
The referenced local statistics helper may be unavailable outside the complete source repository.
It does not calculate email quality scores or independently approve business actions.

use_cases.title: Plan a lifecycle email test
use_cases.description: Create a powered subject-line or call-to-action test with clear metrics, guardrails, and a fixed read date.

use_cases.title: Evaluate campaign results
use_cases.description: Read an ESP export and report effect size, uncertainty, statistical significance, practical significance, and guardrail status.

use_cases.title: Measure incremental revenue
use_cases.description: Design a randomized hold-out that measures conversion or revenue impact against a no-send control.

prompt_templates.title: Design a basic A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test. Baseline open rate is [rate], list size is [size], and meaningful lift is [lift].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a single-variable email test

prompt_templates.title: Plan a send-time test
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a send-time test for [newsletter]. Compare [times], hold content and segment constant, and specify sample size, duration, metrics, and no-peeking rule.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multivariate design
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 2 by 2 test for [factor A] and [factor B]. Use [baseline], [MDE], [alpha], and [power]. Address multiplicity.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a hold-out experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this hold-out export: [results]. Report incremental effect, uncertainty, guardrails, and statistical and practical flags. Apply [owner rule] only when valid.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced read-out with a precommitted decision rule

output_examples.input: Design a subject-line test with a 40% open baseline, 12,000 recipients, and a three-point minimum effect.
output_examples.output: Mode: A/B subject-line test. Use two randomized cells of about 4,300 recipients, hold all other content constant, and read after the full send cycle.

output_examples.input: Compare Tuesday morning and Thursday afternoon for a weekly newsletter.
output_examples.output: Mode: send-time test. Randomly split the audience, hold content constant, compare equal engagement windows, and cover a complete weekday cycle.

output_examples.input: Control had 1,900 opens from 5,000 deliveries. Variant had 2,050 opens from 5,000 deliveries.
output_examples.output: The variant improves opens by 3.0 points. The approximate 95% interval is 1.1 to 4.9 points. The business decision remains undecided without an owner rule.

best_practices: Precommit the primary metric, minimum effect, alpha, power, sample size, and read date.
Change one variable per A/B cell and retain a randomized control.
Review practical impact and unsubscribe, complaint, and bounce guardrails alongside statistical significance.
anti_patterns: Do not change several variables in one A/B cell.
Do not stop early because an interim result appears favorable.
Do not declare a business winner without a named owner and precommitted action rule.

faq.question: Which experiment modes are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports A/B, multivariate, send-time, and randomized hold-out experiments.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It designs experiments and evaluates results, but it does not deploy campaigns.

faq.question: Which data is required?
faq.answer: Planning needs a baseline, list size or send volume, and meaningful lift. Read-outs need delivered counts and outcome counts.

faq.question: Are ESP API credentials required?
faq.answer: No. Manual exports are sufficient, and keyed ESP integrations are optional.

faq.question: Does the skill choose the business action?
faq.answer: It applies only a precommitted rule with a named owner. Otherwise, it reports the decision as undecided.

faq.question: What happens when the audience is too small?
faq.answer: It recommends a larger detectable effect, a longer run, fewer cells, or no test.
